intro.text: After the North Bridge rescue, Kabir travelled to his ancestral village. Tonight he called about a blue door and three knocks. Then the call went silent. I’m taking my motorbike to find him.
intro.speaker: harpreet

sign.text: Neem Village. Three kilometres ahead. The warning below says: When the bell rings at midnight, do not open the blue door. Someone scratched out the last word.
sign.speaker: harpreet

headlight.text: Fog across the canal. There are no other headlights. The village is very quiet.
headlight.speaker: harpreet

rideOut.text: Come on, old bike. One more trip. The fog is thick, and I swear somebody just crossed the road ahead of me.
rideOut.speaker: harpreet

arrival.text: There it is. Neem Lane. Three dark houses and an abandoned well. I’ll park the bike and search on foot.
arrival.speaker: harpreet

rideBack.text: I can retrace the road, but Kabir is still somewhere in this village. I shouldn’t leave without him.
rideBack.speaker: harpreet

laneLook.text: One warm window, one silent loom, and one blue door that looks freshly painted. Kabir said to listen for three knocks.
laneLook.speaker: harpreet

bibiFirst.text: You are looking for Kabir? He came here after the rain, looking pale. Someone kept knocking from the house with the blue door. Take the lantern on my step. Don’t go down there alone.
bibiFirst.speaker: meena

bibiAgain.text: The blue door frightened even the dogs. The first clue is on my wall. Then ask what the weaver saw.
bibiAgain.speaker: meena

marks.text: Three chalk strokes beside a drawing of a staircase going DOWN. Kabir must have made these. He draws the same little arrow in his notes.
marks.speaker: harpreet

marksAgain.text: Three strokes, then an arrow down. The mark points beneath a staircase.
marksAgain.speaker: harpreet

lantern.text: Bibi’s lantern still has oil. I can carry it and use it to see down the old well.
lantern.speaker: harpreet

loom.text: The loom stopped in mid-weave. Red wool was pulled toward the blue-door house, and a shoe print in wet clay points in the same direction.
loom.speaker: harpreet

loomAgain.text: That red thread was dragged toward the blue door. The footsteps match Kabir’s boots.
loomAgain.speaker: harpreet

thread.text: A strong length of red wool. Thin enough to reach beneath a door latch without breaking. I’ll take it.
thread.speaker: harpreet

shadow.text: A tall shadow passes the window. Wait... it’s the loom’s loose curtain swaying in the wind. Still gave me a fright.
shadow.speaker: harpreet

bell.text: The well bell is moving without wind. One... two... three knocks echo from under the lane. Someone is signalling from below.
bell.speaker: harpreet

bellAgain.text: Three knocks. Bibi’s staircase drawing. They both point underground.
bellAgain.speaker: harpreet

wellDark.text: The bucket is too deep to see. I can hear a chain moving, but the darkness hides what is below.
wellDark.speaker: harpreet

wellLit.text: The lantern catches a glint in the bucket! An iron key on a string. If I turn the winch, I might bring it up.
wellLit.speaker: harpreet

crankDark.text: I can’t tell whether the bucket holds anything. I should shine the lantern down first.
crankDark.speaker: harpreet

keyFound.text: I’ve pulled up a cold iron key. Its blue paint matches the door on Neem Lane.
keyFound.speaker: harpreet

crankAgain.text: Nothing left in the bucket except rainwater.
crankAgain.speaker: harpreet

gateLocked.text: The blue door is locked from the street. There’s a narrow iron keyhole under the handle.
gateLocked.speaker: harpreet

gateOpen.text: The iron key turns. The blue door groans open. The house smells of rain, old wood, and candle smoke.
gateOpen.speaker: harpreet

gateOpenAgain.text: The blue door is open. Kabir’s trail leads inside.
gateOpenAgain.speaker: harpreet

portrait.text: The portrait is hanging crooked. Beneath it someone has carved three little marks and a downward arrow. The same symbol as Bibi’s wall.
portrait.speaker: harpreet

clock.text: The hallway clock stopped at midnight. But there’s fresh mud on the stairs, and the handrail is clean where somebody grabbed it.
clock.speaker: harpreet

latchStuck.text: A hatch under the staircase! Its latch is out of reach through a narrow gap. I need something thin and strong to pull it open.
latchStuck.speaker: harpreet

latchOpen.text: The red wool caught the latch. One careful pull and the hatch springs free. The knocking is louder now.
latchOpen.speaker: harpreet

latchAgain.text: The latch is released. I can open the passage now.
latchAgain.speaker: harpreet

missingClues.text: Before I choose a passage, I need to connect Bibi’s marks, the weaver’s trail, and the sounds at the well.
missingClues.speaker: harpreet

choose.text: The floor hides three passages. Which way did Kabir go?
choose.speaker: harpreet

retry.text: That way is silent. Think about the marks pointing DOWN, the dragged thread, and the three knocks under the lane.
retry.speaker: harpreet

cantCombine.text: That doesn’t fit. I should use the lantern at the well, the iron key at the blue door, and the thread on the stuck hatch.
cantCombine.speaker: harpreet

findKabir.text: Harpreet! Thank goodness. I followed the knocks and found a little boy trapped in the cellar after the rain. Then the hatch jammed above us.
findKabir.speaker: kabir

rescued.text: I’ve got you both. That lantern on the stairs is the way out. The knocks were your signal. The scary shadows were only wind and old machinery.
rescued.speaker: harpreet

lastWhisper.text: Yes... I knocked three times. But Harpreet, someone knocked back from the empty house across the lane. I never found out who.
lastWhisper.speaker: kabir

after.text: Kabir is safe. The boy is home. But someone else is awake in Neem Village, and this mystery isn’t finished yet.
after.speaker: harpreet

saveResume.text: I still need to find Kabir. I left my motorbike by Neem Lane; I can continue searching the houses.
saveResume.speaker: harpreet
